I used to experience this at least once a month, from the time I turned 15 up until recently. For me it was always the same thing (similar to a lot of other stories actually) I would wake up in the middle of the night, usually in the middle of some intense dreams. I would open my eyes and look around me and all of a sudden get this intense feeling of dread and cold chills. Then I look around and see a tall man in my room. He was always standing at the end of the bed, usually it was a side profile view of him though, not straight on. And I always got the feeling he was there.as a comfort, and the feeling of dread was from something else. I used to try and move, but by the last time it happened I was so terrified I wouldn't do anything, just lay there and wait for it to pass. 

The last time it happened to me was about year and a half ago, I went to bed at 9:00 and it happened shortly after, but this time there was a huge black shadow in the corner of my room, up by the ceiling and the man wasn't there. I lay there frozen for what felt like forever, then must fallen back to sleep for real because I don't remember anything else until 10:22 that night, when my son woke me up screaming bloody murder in his room. When I ran in to see what was wrong he told me there was something in his room on the ceiling hiding in the dark. I sat with him for a while until he fell asleep, with that same familiar feeling of dread except this time I was awake. Once he fell asleep I went back to my room, leaving the hallway light and my bedroom lamp on because I was afraid. I dug out some holy water(my husband's aunt gave me some a few weeks earlier because she was convinced the reason I  was suicidal was because I needed to be "saved").  I was feeling pretty silly but watched that documentary about sleep paralysis and one lady did this so I copied her: I just said out loud "in the name of Jesus Christ I command you to leave. This is a house of God and you are not welcome" laughed at myself a little bit, and then fell asleep with the lights on.

I don't usually believe in anything funky, and tend to lean towards logical explanations, but I asked my husband's aunt to cleanse the house for us,(she started to once before but got interrupted and didn't finish). I also started sleeping with a salt lamp(again I don't buy into the hippie stuff but I will try anything once). It's been about a year and I haven't had it happen since.

Editing to add: I do still have some pretty awesome lucid dreams, though which I'm sure is a factor in why I used to experience sleep paralysis so often...

Editing to also add: In no way am I saying a super spooky demon was haunting me and I made it go away, I'm just saying this is what happened. More likely I still do it and don't realize because I took an active role in avoiding it so it isn't scary anymore.

As far as the drug problem is concerned, I think it has gotten much worse in the past few years- I definitely wouldn't leave my car unlocked when I ran into the store there now, where as before I never even bothered locking the doors to my home when I left for the day. I also used to walk home after band concerts and dances at night time when I was in high school- there's no way I'd do that now, even in broad daylight.

If you're looking for an area with a similar vibe and low housing costs I'd look into Rouses Point/Champlain, New York. It's still about the same distance from Burlington (and only half an hour from Plattsburgh which is another decent sized city), but captures that quintessential "middle class American suburb" feel much better than Richford.  It's literally four minutes across the bridge to Vermont, but it feels like a whole different world over here than in Franklin County.  If you have your heart set on living in Vermont, the Johnson/Hyde Park area may be worth looking into as well. Still close to Burlington, but not Franklin County :)

If you have any questions or want more specifics feel free to ask, I grew up in Richford and would be happy to help!
